mappings.note: Explains oligarchy as rule by a small powerful group. Comparative government under the goal.
Reads the table to identify which forms of government lack universal adult franchise. The equal right to vote is the axis of the question, so LO-175.
Why democracy is preferred over dictatorship or monarchy - equal rights, freedom, accountability. The equality argument carries it, as with the other 'why democracy' items.
Two challenges democracies face. The working of democracy under the goal.
How citizens keep democracy strong. Civic participation under the goal.
What sovereignty means for a country. A constitutional term under the goal.
The three functions of government worked through the school-committee analogy. Institutions of government under the goal.
Direct against representative democracy and why the latter suits large nations. Comparative government.
The executive-legislature relationship in India against the United States. Comparative institutions under the goal.

The Uttaramerur inscriptions as evidence of early local democracy (CG-SST3) and the question of what such an inscription cannot tell us, which is source criticism (CG-SST2). The item asks for both the significance and the limitations.
Rajadharma as a check on royal power. The chapter's argument about limits on authority, so the civics goal.
Compares where power comes from and what limits it in an absolute monarchy and a dictatorship. Comparative government.
What sets a theocracy apart from democracy and monarchy. Comparative government under the goal.
How a democracy can drift towards oligarchy. A judgement about forms of government; the cartoon is only the prompt, so LO-182 would misread it.
The importance of fundamental rights such as freedom of speech and equality to a working democracy. Equality is named in the question, so LO-175.
Names separation of powers as the principle keeping the organs independent. A constitutional principle under the goal.
Names a gana-sangha mahajanapada as an early republic. Early democratic practice, kept in the civics lane as the chapter presents it.
Names the Uttaramerur inscriptions as the record of village sabha elections. Local democratic process under the goal.
Names monarchy from its hereditary ruler. Comparative government.
Names theocracy from rule by religious law and leaders. Comparative government.
Names dictatorship from absolute, unlimited power. Comparative government.
Names oligarchy from rule by a small wealthy group. Completes the set of government-type recalls.
Lists three roles of modern governments. Functions of government under the goal.
Why representation beats direct participation in a large group, argued from the school committee. Comparative democratic practice.
Explains the legislative, executive and judicial functions. The organs of government under the goal.
Four aspects on which forms of government differ. Comparative government under the goal.
What equality means as a democratic principle. The equality outcome stated directly.
The importance of universal adult franchise in a representative democracy. Political equality, in line with the other franchise items.
Why an independent judiciary is essential. An institution of democracy, so the goal.
Independent judiciary protecting rights, with a trailing part contrasting collective decision-making with a monarchy of the era. Institutions and comparative government, so the goal.

A constitutional monarchy where a press-freedom law is tested by courts and civil society. Institutions and safeguards of democracy, so the goal; the right threatened is press freedom rather than equality.
A coup suspending the constitution, dissolving parliament and controlling media has to be named and judged. Comparative government and democratic institutions under the goal.

Corporate lobbying shaping laws is asked to be recognised as an oligarchic drift (CG-SST3), and part (ii) asks which democratic principle it undermines - the equal weight of every citizen's voice (LO-175).
A dispute in the Vajji sabha, how a gana-sangha would settle it and how a monarchy would differ. Early democratic process and comparative government, so the goal.
